## The True Cost of Hiring

SHRM puts the average cost-per-hire at $4,700, but this number dramatically understates reality for many organizations. When you include all costs, the true figure is often 2-3x higher.

### What Gets Missed

Most cost-per-hire calculations include:

- Job board postings
- Agency fees (if used)
- Background checks

But they often miss:

- Recruiter salary (allocated per hire)
- Hiring manager time
- Interview team time
- Offer and negotiation time
- Onboarding costs
- Productivity ramp-up

### The Complete Formula

True Cost-Per-Hire = (External Costs + Internal Costs) / Total Hires

External Costs:

- Job boards and advertising
- Agency or vendor fees
- Background checks and assessments
- Recruitment marketing
- ATS and tool subscriptions

Internal Costs:

- Recruiter salary and benefits (percentage of time)
- Hiring manager time (hours multiplied by hourly cost)
- Interview panel time
- HR and onboarding staff time
- Training and ramp-up investment

### A Real Example

Let us calculate for a mid-market company hiring 50 people per year:

| Cost Category | Annual Total | Per Hire |
|---|---|---|
| Job boards | $50,000 | $1,000 |
| One recruiter | $80,000 | $1,600 |
| Manager time (10 hrs/hire at $75/hr) | $37,500 | $750 |
| Interview time (5 hrs x 4 people at $50/hr) | $50,000 | $1,000 |
| Onboarding | $25,000 | $500 |
| Total | $242,500 | $4,850 |

This does not include agency fees. Add even occasional agency use, and costs skyrocket. Compare this to subscription pricing .

- Faster fills: less manager time spent waiting
- Higher quality: fewer bad hires to replace

### Strategies for Reducing Cost-Per-Hire

- Improve source quality: stop spending on low-converting channels
- Speed up the process: time is money for everyone involved
- Build referral programs: lowest cost-per-hire source
- Invest in employer brand: reduces need for expensive sourcing
- Use subscription sourcing: predictable costs, aligned incentives

### Track and Optimize

Measure cost-per-hire quarterly. Break it down by department, role type, and source. Identify outliers and address root causes.

The goal is not just lower costs. It is better ROI on your talent investment.
